why_this_file_exists: ledger-*.json and sacm-*.json are gitignored, so the numbers they carry would not survive the commit. This is a small, committable transcription of the three runs, plus two recomputations made independently of the artifacts themselves.

ledger.note: The ledger is quadratic in Ctx.resolve, but at 1955 functions it finished in 3 s, not the 363 s Django needed. It is not a bottleneck at this size.

goals.G2 semantics+transpiler agree with the r: UNDEVELOPED (conformance.json absent: no differential run exists for any C corpus)
goals.G3 every function translated without hol: UNSUPPORTED (1263/1955 functions carry at least one hole)
goals.G5 theorems kernel-checked, no unsound a: UNDEVELOPED (no theorems about LinuxCrypto exist, and no module-scoped axiom dump)

defeaters.D3.1: REFUTED BY EXECUTION: 136 of the 318 claimed-core functions hole when run.
defeaters.D3: Func.total is computed from the AST it describes; undefeated except where execution looked.

assurance_case.note: sacm.py reads the fixed filename core-oracle.json and requires its module tag to match, so it was run with --root pointing at a scratch directory holding ast-LinuxCrypto.json, ledger-LinuxCrypto.json and core-oracle-LinuxCrypto.json copied to core-oracle.json. Run from the repo root it reports G3.2 UNSUPPORTED / coverage 0% because the repo-root core-oracle.json is tagged Cachetools. That provenance check is correct behaviour, not a bug; the per-module filename is the gap.

execution_oracle.inputs: synthetic only, 12 per function, fuel 5000, seed 20260819
execution_oracle.real_input_reason: core_oracle.py derives real arguments by tracing a Python test suite with differential.py's tracer. LinuxCrypto is C kernel code with no runnable in-tree suite reachable from here, so every input is synthetic. Zero real-input evidence: no claim here rests on a recorded call.

comparison_cachetools.note: Python. The C ratio is LOWER, but only because C's static core is already tiny (318/1955 = 16% vs 74/238 = 31%) and, as the recomputation below shows, mostly empty.

execution_oracle.shape_caveat: 29 of the 136 refutations hole only with labels of the form field:X:non-object / setField:X:non-object, i.e. because a synthetic int was passed where the C code expects a pointer to a struct. Those are weaker evidence: the apparatus chose the shape. The other 107 hole on constructs (unop:-, control:FOR, op:indirection:pointer, op:alloc:array-decl, call:<untranslated callee>) that no choice of argument avoids.
execution_oracle.call_closure_refuted: Labels of the form call:crypto_skcipher_reqtfm, call:ahash_request_ctx, call:kpp_tfm_ctx are callee resolutions that failed at runtime inside functions the ledger declared CALL-CLOSED. Static call closure is itself overstated here, not just hole-freedom.

independent_recomputation.method: Recomputed from ast-LinuxCrypto.json, not from the oracle's own output: classify each surviving function by whether its body is semantically empty (skip, or a seq of skips).
independent_recomputation.reading: Every empty-body function in the module lands in the survivor set, and they make up 85% of it. An empty body cannot hole; it also cannot be evidence. The honest verifiable core of LinuxCrypto is 28 functions out of 1955 (1.4%), several of them the crypto_null no-ops (null_crypt, null_final, null_setkey, skcipher_noexport). Against that denominator the static claim of 318 overstates by 11.4x, not 1.75x.
independent_recomputation.empty_bodies_are_a_transpiler_artifact: Joern materialises kernel macros and declarations (EXPORT_SYMBOL, DEFINE_MUTEX, MODULE_ALIAS_CRYPTO, DECLARE_WORK, per-file <global> nodes) as functions with no body. They are counted in all three of the 1955 / 692 / 318 figures.

tool_fix.bug: The Lean harness called `applyFunc ctx fuel h fn self args` — a signature that no longer exists: applyFunc gained a trailing `List (String x Val)` keyword-argument parameter. The scratch module failed to elaborate, so Lean answered nothing for every case and each one was bucketed as no_answer. The run would have reported 318/318 INCONCLUSIVE, 0 refuted, on a corpus where 136 functions actually hole.
tool_fix.fix: pass [] for kwargs, and add a SMOKE GATE: the first case must produce an answer or the run aborts with Lean's diagnostics printed, instead of reporting a core-wide silence as a result.
tool_fix.unfixed_elsewhere: scripts/differential.py line ~1557 emits the same stale call and is owned by another agent this session. It was not touched. Any differential/conformance run for any module will fail there until it is updated.
